attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, written in the first person.

semantics.note: The testable core is the causal clause: Claude beats LaMDA because it has more data. The sentience clause is kept as his personal judgment. Neither part is broadened.

contract.note: Asking for comparable data disclosures and controlled comparisons is a fair test of a specific causal claim. Reading 'because' as a contributing cause, not the only cause, is ordinary and does not stretch his words.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure of Claude 3.7's data sources and methods. It gives no data volume and no comparison with LaMDA.
Anthropic's own release announcement with performance claims. It has no LaMDA comparison and does not isolate the effect of data.

reviews.rationale: Neither item gives comparable training-data volumes or a controlled Claude–LaMDA comparison, so the evidence can neither confirm nor refute that more data explains Claude's advantage. The packet's own gaps say the same.

attribution.note: He quotes his own June 2022 essay and endorses it again, saying it still applies to Claude.

semantics.note: The proposition matches his statement. Extending it from LaMDA to language models generally is backed by his line that it all still applies to Claude.

contract.note: His context (Searle's Chinese Room, Moore's point about relating sentences to the world) is about semantic grounding. The contract reads 'connect to the world' as tool retrieval, which pulls in more text. That reading is stretched against him and decides the result.

evidence.note: The 2022 LaMDA paper describes a retrieval toolset. That shows functional tool use, not semantic grounding.

Anthropic's dated announcement of Claude web search before the post. Under the contract's reading it would contradict the claim, but retrieving web text does not settle the grounding claim he actually made.

reviews.rationale: The contract's retrieval reading is not the ordinary reading of his argument, which is about grounding words in the world. Read fairly, nothing in the packet settles the claim. The packet itself admits retrieval cannot decide the philosophical reading.

attribution.note: Marcus's own aside in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps his scope: Anthropic disrespects the rights of creators whose work it takes. It does not claim that every use infringed.

contract.note: Taking the factual copyright side of 'respect the rights' and keeping acquisition separate from fair-use training is a fair, ordinary reading. Using later court findings about conduct before the post is reasonable.

evidence.note: June 2025 court order records Anthropic's 2022 acquisition of pirated books and rules this was not excused by fair use. The conduct predates the post and the order predates the evaluation date.
The same order rules that purchased copies and training use were fair use. This limits the claim's breadth but does not cancel the finding on pirated copies.

reviews.rationale: A court found Anthropic knowingly took pirated books before the post and was not entitled to keep them in its library under fair use. That meets the support condition for writers. The order covers book authors only, not other artists, and is not a final liability judgment.

attribution.note: He quotes his own 2022 essay and endorses it again as applying to today's LLMs.

semantics.note: His categorical wording ('no more and no less', 'without any coherent understanding') is kept, along with the qualifier that it applies to current LLMs.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 'no coherent, generalizable representations of situations' is an ordinary reading. 'Coherent understanding' has no threshold, though, so how strictly it is read drives the result.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own research on its model: interventions on intermediate concepts change Claude's answers. This cuts against 'just word sequences', but it is a company disclosure with stated limits and no independent replication.
Peer-authored preprint finding that apparent world models are much less coherent than diagnostics suggest. It does not show that every covered model lacks all understanding.

reviews.rationale: The evidence points both ways. A company's own unreplicated interpretability work suggests some structured representations. Independent work shows world models are brittle and incoherent. Neither settles the categorical claim without a threshold, and the packet's gaps say so.
